course_name_original: ELECTRICAL, HYDRAULIC AND PNEUMATIC DRIVE UNITS (B010638)
course_name_en: ELECTRICAL, HYDRAULIC AND PNEUMATIC DRIVE UNITS
prerequisites: basics of mechanical and electrical engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Consolidate a systematic knowledge of the key aspects necessary for the design and analysis of drive systems.
Acquire in-depth knowledge of the principles of electrotechnics that govern electric drives and of the control methods used in industrial plants.

Develop the capacity for mechanical study of components and systems, including the understanding of the application context, correct sizing, and graphical representation of systems, essential for technical documentation.
Be able to choose and use appropriate components, fully understanding their limitations and potential applications in electrical and fluidic fields.

Be capable of identifying, formulating, and solving complex problems in the design of drive systems. This includes defining specifications, technical constraints, but also considering social, health and safety, environmental, and commercial aspects.
Be able to create complete engineering projects, appropriate to the developed level of knowledge and understanding.
Develop the ability to choose and apply appropriate analytical and modeling methods to simulate the behavior of components and systems, in order to predict and improve their performance.
Development of the ability to work in a coordinated manner on complex projects.
Ability to develop a rigorous technical discussion, providing adequate arguments for design choices.
Acquisition of proficiency in graphical representation and communication (drafting of diagrams, graphs, and tables), a fundamental language in fluidics.
Understanding and application of relevant technical standards, particularly those related to the safety and installation of systems.

syllabus_topics: Generation and distribution of compressed air
Compressed air and compressed air treatment
Compressed air distribution: networks and flexible connections
Pneumatic cylinders: description, static and dynamic sizing
Pneumatic valves: Direction-controlling valves (types, name, drive, connection)
Working fluids: general characteristics, viscosity dependence on temperature and pressure, viscometers, modulus of compressibility, flame retardant types
Hydraulic power generation, pumps construction types
Linear actuators: main types and basic equations
Example of maximum size of cylinder-pump circuit
Hydraulic motors: construction types, measures for proper functioning of pistons in fixed radial and axial piston motors
Hydraulic motors: basic equations, sample calculations on a hydraulic circuit
Directional valves: seat valves, rotary and tray
Covering static and transient in tray distributors
Operating range of spool valves, types of implementation of distributors, valves for controlling pressure and flow, check valves
Examples of hydraulic circuits to drive motors and cylinders
Accumulators for hydraulic circuits, choice and design
Structure of an electric servo: converter, motor, controller, transducers, transmission, load
Motion control requirements: variation, control, following
Specifications of needs in a control problem
Motion control techniques: velocity, position, torque
Open and closed loop control layouts
Description of the main typologies of electric servomechanisms
Motor-load coupling: Introduction, direct coupling or through a gearbox, direct and retrograde motion
Motor characteristic curves: Speed generator, Torque generator, Power generator
Functioning as motor, brake or generator (example: lift), Power flux associated
Locus of loads: definition, locus of static loads, locus of dynamic loads, RMS values of torque and angular speed
Direct motor-load coupling, regime condition, transient
Effect of the gear ratio: Introduction, power losses, direct and retrograde power flux, reduction of torques and inertia, regime, transient, the flywheel
Verification and choice of the motor size
Choice of the motor and of the gearbox
Choice of the motor and of the reduction ratio for static load at constant speed
Choice of the motor and of the reduction ratio for static load at variable speed, Adaptation of operational fields, Gearboxes
Choice of the motor and of the reduction ratio for limited duration loads
Choice of the motor and of the reduction ratio for dynamic loads
Simple motion laws for cyclic movements: Judgment parameters, Cycloidal motion law and with constant acceleration, Comparison
Improved motion laws: Seven stretches motion law with linear acceleration
Thermal problem for electric actuators: Introduction
Thermal balance of an electric motor
Regime thermal behavior, nominal torque and power
Thermal behavior during a transient with a constant load
Thermal behavior: arbitrary and standard services
Overload of motor, converter and protections
assessment_rules: The oral exam focuses on course topics, including fundamentals of fluid power components and electric actuators, and the discussion of a practical problem concerning the design or analysis of a complex system of actuators. The exam assesses knowledge and skills (cc3, cc5, cc6, ca3, ca5, ca6). Grading is based on conceptual understanding, application ability, independence, and communication. A grade of 18-22 signifies elementary knowledge, while 29-30 and Honors denote complete, in-depth knowledge, independent operation, and critical thinking.
